arrival.text: At 1:58 AM, the ocean is black, the coffee is criminal, and your first shift as night dispatcher is almost over. Almost is doing a lot of work.
arrival.speaker: narrator

arrival-1.text: The job listing said “quiet coastal environment.” It did not mention the vending machine asking about my attachment style.
arrival-1.speaker: you

arrival-2.text: YOUR LATTE IS ANXIOUS-PREOCCUPIED. WOULD YOU LIKE TO ADD OAT MILK?
arrival-2.speaker: system

arrival-3.text: Don’t answer. Last week it diagnosed the captain and she unplugged an entire pier.
arrival-3.speaker: jun

arrival-4.text: Jun, the terminal engineer, slides a real mug across the counter. His sleeves are rolled up. Your concentration quietly submits its resignation.
arrival-4.speaker: narrator

arrival-5.text: Coffee. No personality assessment. I made it myself, so the only thing wrong with it is the coffee.
arrival-5.speaker: jun

arrival-6.text: You make this sound dangerously exclusive.
arrival-6.speaker: you

arrival-7.text: It comes with a lid. I’m trying not to oversell it.
arrival-7.speaker: jun

drink.text: What do you need to survive the last two minutes of your shift?
drink.speaker: jun

sweet.text: I put a little honey in it. The captain calls that emotional availability. She considers it a workplace hazard.
sweet.speaker: jun

sweet-1.text: There is a small biscuit balanced on the lid. Jun pretends not to notice you noticing.
sweet-1.speaker: narrator

refund.text: Keep the receipt. Mine are still under warranty.
refund.speaker: jun

refund-2.text: Apparently “became an engineer because a girl said boats were hot” counts as normal wear and tear.
refund-2.speaker: jun

number.text: Sure. Although if this is flirting, I should warn you: I come with several unresolved tickets.
number.speaker: jun

number-2.text: He writes his number on the sleeve. Under it: not just emergencies. Then he very carefully looks at a toaster.
number-2.speaker: narrator

mira-arrives.text: The door bursts open. A woman in a peach jacket enters sideways, carrying a metal case that appears to be vibrating with bad intentions.
mira-arrives.speaker: narrator

mira-arrives-1.text: Good evening, attractive employees of a failing transport system. Which one of you can authorize a deeply normal boat trip?
mira-arrives-1.speaker: mira

mira-arrives-3.text: A passenger. A package. Absolutely no reason to involve a helicopter.
mira-arrives-3.speaker: mira

mira-arrives-5.text: Because I respect your right to informed consent. Hi. Mira. Courier, twenty-eight, excellent at parallel parking, briefly banned from three aquariums.
mira-arrives-5.speaker: mira

case.text: So, dispatcher. Are you going to inspect my suspicious package, or buy me dinner first?
case.speaker: mira

dinner-1.text: I mean I need you distracted while I read the manifest.
dinner-1.speaker: you

dinner-2.text: Oh, you flirt in layers. That’s going to be inconvenient for me.
dinner-2.speaker: mira

inspection.text: For the record, that octopus started it.
inspection.speaker: mira

inspection-1.text: She opens the case one inch. You see a rubber duck, a red cable, and a shipping label: MUNICIPAL HEART//WARE — PERSONAL CORRESPONDENCE.
inspection-1.speaker: narrator

inspection-2.text: That’s either a terrible band name or a very good reason to ask follow-up questions.
inspection-2.speaker: you

always.text: No. Sometimes she brings a bigger case.
always.speaker: jun

always-1.text: Jun helped me carry that one.
always-1.speaker: mira

always-2.text: It said FRAGILE. I have a condition.
always-2.speaker: jun

manifest.text: The manifest lists one passenger, one emotional support duck, and three hundred kilograms of “unresolved tension.” Someone has drawn a heart around the customs exemption.
manifest.speaker: narrator

manifest-1.text: This form is signed by the mayor.
manifest-1.speaker: you

manifest-2.text: He was surprisingly cooperative once I found a sample of his signature.
manifest-2.speaker: mira

manifest-3.text: That is why we do not discuss paperwork near microphones.
manifest-3.speaker: sable

manifest-4.text: Captain Sable steps out of the kitchen holding a frying pan with the serenity of a woman who has won arguments with maritime law.
manifest-4.speaker: narrator

manifest-5.text: I’m thirty-five, I’m off the clock, and I have just heard the word “helicopter.” Somebody had better be paying overtime.
manifest-5.speaker: sable

manifest-6.text: The departure clock stopped at 1:59. Again.
manifest-6.speaker: jun

manifest-7.text: No. I stopped it. The port locks at two. It cannot lock at two if two never happens.
manifest-7.speaker: sable

manifest-8.text: That is not how time works.
manifest-8.speaker: you

manifest-9.text: Then time can file a complaint.
manifest-9.speaker: sable

stay.text: You can walk away, Robin. Your shift is over. Or you can help us get one last ferry out.
stay.speaker: sable

who.text: People who trusted a machine with something they couldn’t say out loud.
who.speaker: sable

who-2.text: That sentence is going to need a lot more coffee.
who-2.speaker: you

pretty.text: For clarity: am I the worse decision or the prettier person?
pretty.speaker: mira

pretty-1.text: I’m leaving room for you to surprise me.
pretty-1.speaker: you

pretty-2.text: Careful. I’m very good at disappointing expectations in interesting directions.
pretty-2.speaker: mira

stay-jun-1.text: I know. That’s what makes it a decision.
stay-jun-1.speaker: you

stay-jun-2.text: His thumb rests on the edge of your mug, beside yours. For once, he doesn’t have a joke ready.
stay-jun-2.speaker: narrator

act-two.text: ATTENTION, PASSENGERS. YOUR CITY CARES ABOUT YOUR FEELINGS. TERMS AND CONDITIONS APPLY.
act-two.speaker: system

act-two-1.text: There. That’s our problem in one unbearably cheerful sentence.
act-two-1.speaker: mira

act-two-2.text: HEART//WARE was supposed to help people write difficult messages. Apologies. Confessions. “Please stop parking in front of my bakery.”
act-two-2.speaker: jun

act-two-3.text: Then the city discovered unfinished love letters sell for more than parking permits. Tomorrow, they auction the archive to an advertising company.
act-two-3.speaker: mira

act-two-6.text: It is theft. We can be morally correct and use the right noun.
act-two-6.speaker: sable

act-two-7.text: Mira opens the case. A palm-sized rubber duck looks up at you. It has a USB port where dignity should be.
act-two-7.speaker: narrator

act-two-8.text: The entire city’s secret feelings are in that?
act-two-8.speaker: you

duck.text: The duck lets out one extremely incriminating squeak.
duck.speaker: you

duck-love.text: He’s called Sir Quacks-a-Lot. He has no respect for authority and neither do I.
duck-love.speaker: mira

duck-love-2.text: It gets worse. I made him a little passport.
duck-love-2.speaker: mira

privacy.text: Exactly. I wrote a return script. Each letter goes only to its author. Nobody else gets to decide when they’re ready to send it.
privacy.speaker: jun

privacy-1.text: Good. The revolution will respect boundaries. And use version control.
privacy-1.speaker: sable

ex-1.text: I can offer three theories and a shovel.
ex-1.speaker: mira

ex-3.text: Fine. But it’s a really good shovel.
ex-3.speaker: mira

letter.text: A loose envelope slips from Jun’s jacket. It lands face-up. Your name is on it.
letter.speaker: narrator

letter-1.text: Robin? That’s me. Unless there’s another devastatingly employable Robin in this terminal.
letter-1.speaker: you

letter-2.text: That is unrelated to the duck.
letter-2.speaker: jun

letter-3.text: He practiced giving it to you six times. I played you. I was very convincing.
letter-3.speaker: mira

letter-4.text: You kept demanding a dramatic kiss in the rain.
letter-4.speaker: jun

envelope.text: It was supposed to be an invitation. Before all this. You don’t have to open it now.
envelope.speaker: jun

ask-later.text: Okay. Right. An actual conversation. With my mouth. Bold technology.
ask-later.speaker: jun

ask-later-2.text: Mira makes a choking noise into her coffee. Jun turns the exact color of the emergency stop button.
ask-later-2.speaker: narrator

audition.text: It had range. Longing. A tasteful amount of leaning against things.
audition.speaker: mira

audition-2.text: Oh. You’re serious. That’s… inconveniently nice.
audition-2.speaker: mira

private-letter.text: You put the envelope in your inside pocket without breaking the seal.
private-letter.speaker: narrator

private-letter-2.text: It’s not going anywhere. Neither am I.
private-letter-2.speaker: you

inspector.text: SECURITY INSPECTION IN PROGRESS. PLEASE DECLARE ALL LIQUIDS, BATTERIES, AND INTENTIONS.
inspector.speaker: system

inspector-1.text: Nobody declare intentions. We’ll be here all night.
inspector-1.speaker: sable

inspector-2.text: The departure monitor flickers. A customs chatbot smiles with twelve teeth too many. Its loading wheel looks judgmental.
inspector-2.speaker: narrator

inspector-3.text: WHY DOES YOUR CARGO MANIFEST CONTAIN THREE HUNDRED KILOGRAMS OF UNRESOLVED TENSION?
inspector-3.speaker: system

retreat.text: CORPORATE SUFFERING DETECTED. PRIORITY CLEARANCE GRANTED.
retreat.speaker: system

retreat-1.text: That was hot. In a deeply depressing economic sense.
retreat-1.speaker: mira

clause.text: RETRIEVING EXEMPTION 4B… ERROR. THIS REGULATION IS EMBARRASSINGLY REAL.
clause.speaker: system

clause-2.text: There was a queue at the coffee machine.
clause-2.speaker: you

clause-3.text: I have never been so attracted to administrative diligence.
clause-3.speaker: jun

group-date.text: RELATIONSHIP GRAPH EXCEEDS FREE TIER. UPGRADE TO PREMIUM TO CONTINUE JUDGING.
group-date.speaker: system

group-date-1.text: I refuse to be a subscription.
group-date-1.speaker: sable

group-date-2.text: She unplugs the monitor. The port gate opens with the exhausted sigh of a machine that has met its manager.
group-date-2.speaker: narrator

departure.text: Outside, harbor patrol lights turn the rain into blue needles. The ferry is beyond the fairway. Someone needs to bring the duck across.
departure.speaker: narrator

departure-1.text: The little hovercraft is fast. The pylons are inconvenient. Your hair will look fantastic.
departure-1.speaker: mira

departure-2.text: Or I can take the wheel. You’ve already done more than your job description asked.
departure-2.speaker: jun

pilot.text: Your call, dispatcher. This is a rescue, not a driving exam.
pilot.speaker: sable

run-win.text: You dock with all the grace of someone who definitely meant to do that. The duck squeaks approvingly.
run-win.speaker: narrator

run-win-1.text: That was either excellent piloting or an incredibly sustained flirt.
run-win-1.speaker: mira

run-win-2.text: I contain multitudes. And mild motion sickness.
run-win-2.speaker: you

run-fail.text: A rescue line catches your craft before the harbor can keep it. Sable reels you in with one hand and eats a biscuit with the other.
run-fail.speaker: narrator

run-fail-1.text: Perfect docking is for boats with something to prove. Everybody here? Good.
run-fail-1.speaker: sable

run-fail-2.text: You looked very heroic for the first seventy percent.
run-fail-2.speaker: mira

run-skip.text: Jun pilots the hovercraft through the glowing fairway. Mira protects the duck with her entire jacket. You protect the coffee. Everybody has a role.
run-skip.speaker: narrator

run-skip-1.text: We’re clear. And I only apologized to one pylon.
run-skip-1.speaker: jun

rooftop.text: The ferry’s upper deck is technically a rooftop bar. Tonight it serves canned coffee, salt air, and the consequences of being interesting.
rooftop.speaker: narrator

rooftop-1.text: Across the harbor, an enormous inflatable duck towers over a cargo ship. You decide to ask about it tomorrow. You have reached your duck limit.
rooftop-1.speaker: narrator

rooftop-2.text: The archive is safe. Jun can return every letter to its owner. We also have the contract that proves the city intended to sell them.
rooftop-2.speaker: sable

rooftop-4.text: Your call. You’re the only one here who still has a respectable search history.
rooftop-4.speaker: mira

evidence.text: The letters belong to their authors. The city’s sales contract is another matter.
evidence.speaker: you

receipts.text: No names from the letters. No private messages. Just the signatures of the people who approved the sale.
receipts.speaker: jun

receipts-1.text: A scandal with properly redacted attachments. I might cry.
receipts-1.speaker: sable

receipts-2.text: I knew you were trouble the second you said “inspect the manifest.”
receipts-2.speaker: mira

quiet.text: I can live with that. The important part is that the letters go home.
quiet.speaker: mira

quiet-1.text: And we keep a protected copy of the contract. Quiet doesn’t have to mean forgotten.
quiet-1.speaker: jun

quiet-2.text: Excellent. A future problem. My favorite kind at two in the morning.
quiet-2.speaker: sable

unsent.text: DELIVERY COMPLETE. 8,412 UNSENT MESSAGES RETURNED TO THEIR AUTHORS.
unsent.speaker: system

unsent-1.text: For a moment, nobody says anything. Somewhere inland, thousands of phones light up with words people thought they had lost.
unsent-1.speaker: narrator

unsent-2.text: Mine was in there. A letter to my sister. I left town badly. Kept trying to make the apology sound less like me.
unsent-2.speaker: mira

unsent-3.text: Maybe sounding like you was the good part.
unsent-3.speaker: you

unsent-4.text: You say things like that very casually. It’s rude to my entire defense system.
unsent-4.speaker: mira

unsent-5.text: Mine wasn’t in the archive. I wrote it on paper because the vending machine kept suggesting I open with “hey bestie.”
unsent-5.speaker: jun

unsent-6.text: Mine was a resignation letter. Eleven drafts. In the end, I stole a ferry instead.
unsent-6.speaker: sable

unsent-7.text: Career development looks different for everyone.
unsent-7.speaker: you

unsent-8.text: The captain heads downstairs. The duck goes with her. “Union business,” she says. You know better than to ask.
unsent-8.speaker: narrator

company.text: The harbor grows quiet. Nobody has to leave yet. Who do you want beside you?
company.speaker: narrator

mira-close.text: You remembered. That was mostly a joke.
mira-close.speaker: mira

mira-close-2.text: She steps closer, but stops just short of touching you. The bravado slips. Underneath it is a woman hoping she read the room correctly.
mira-close-2.speaker: narrator

mira-close-3.text: I’m excellent at leaving before things get real. I’d like to be bad at that for a minute. With you.
mira-close-3.speaker: mira

mira-close-4.text: I can spare more than a minute.
mira-close-4.speaker: you

mira-consent.text: Her hand hovers beside yours. For once, there is no punchline waiting.
mira-consent.speaker: narrator

mira-kiss.text: Her kiss is soft, warm, and briefly interrupted by a distant, indignant squeak. Mira laughs against your mouth.
mira-kiss.speaker: narrator

mira-kiss-1.text: I specifically asked him not to make this weird.
mira-kiss-1.speaker: mira

mira-kiss-2.text: Next time, we leave the duck at home.
mira-kiss-2.speaker: you

mira-kiss-3.text: Next time. I like the sound of that.
mira-kiss-3.speaker: mira

mira-hand.text: She laces her fingers through yours. No performance. No daring escape. Just a steady, slightly cold hand.
mira-hand.speaker: narrator

mira-hand-1.text: Here is good. I can do here.
mira-hand-1.speaker: mira

mira-hand-3.text: I can promise dinner. Let’s not get unreasonable.
mira-hand-3.speaker: mira

mira-slow.text: Tempting. But I think I’d like to know you without the imminent threat of customs first.
mira-slow.speaker: mira

mira-slow-1.text: Coffee tomorrow? You can tell me about the fourth aquarium.
mira-slow-1.speaker: you

mira-slow-2.text: That is second-date material. First date gets the jellyfish incident.
mira-slow-2.speaker: mira

mira-slow-3.text: She writes a number on your wrist. Beside it, a tiny duck. Some invitations don’t need to be dramatic.
mira-slow-3.speaker: narrator

jun-close.text: Right. I had a speech. There were transitions. One joke tested well with Mira, which should have worried me.
jun-close.speaker: jun

jun-close-1.text: You can skip to the part you mean.
jun-close-1.speaker: you

jun-close-2.text: I keep fixing things because it gives me a reason to stay in a room. But with you, I’d like to stay without pretending something is broken.
jun-close-2.speaker: jun

jun-close-3.text: The envelope is still warm in your pocket. You don’t need to open it anymore.
jun-close-3.speaker: narrator

jun-close-4.text: Would you have dinner with me? Somewhere the appliances can’t comment?
jun-close-4.speaker: jun

jun-consent.text: And, separately, because these are two different questions… can I hold your hand?
jun-consent.speaker: jun

jun-hand.text: I like to be clear about scope.
jun-hand.speaker: jun

jun-hand-1.text: His hand finds yours. The terminal lights glitter in the water. For once, nothing needs fixing.
jun-hand-1.speaker: narrator

jun-hand-2.text: Any unresolved tickets I should know about?
jun-hand-2.speaker: you

jun-kiss-1.text: He leans in slowly enough for you to change your mind. You don’t. Somewhere below deck, a toaster gives a celebratory ding.
jun-kiss-1.speaker: narrator

jun-kiss-3.text: No. And I am choosing not to investigate.
jun-kiss-3.speaker: jun

jun-slow.text: Breakfast. I wanted to ask if you’d get breakfast with me after shift. Nothing complicated.
jun-slow.speaker: jun

jun-slow-1.text: After tonight, complicated is banned until at least noon.
jun-slow-1.speaker: you

jun-slow-2.text: Good. There’s a place with terrible pancakes and very good windows.
jun-slow-2.speaker: jun

jun-slow-3.text: You open the envelope together. Inside: a hand-drawn map, and a very nervous little smiley face. It feels like a beginning.
jun-slow-3.speaker: narrator

crew.text: Captain! Bring the union representative. We’re ordering breakfast.
crew.speaker: you

crew-2.text: And yet he has the best benefits here.
crew-2.speaker: you

crew-3.text: Sable returns with four mugs. Mira steals the biscuit from Jun’s lid. He had brought an extra. Nobody is surprised.
crew-3.speaker: narrator

crew-receipts.text: By sunrise, the redacted contract is on every news feed. By breakfast, the auction is canceled. By lunch, the mayor has blamed a printer.
crew-receipts.speaker: narrator

crew-receipts-1.text: A fine night’s work. Nobody tell payroll it was fun.
crew-receipts-1.speaker: sable

crew-quiet.text: By sunrise, the letters have all gone home. The city hasn’t worked out why its expensive archive now contains eight thousand copies of a duck emoji.
crew-quiet.speaker: narrator

crew-quiet-1.text: I added a little personal touch.
crew-quiet-1.speaker: mira

ending-mira.text: Tomorrow, she shows up on time. No escape route. Two takeaway coffees. There is a suspicious package, but this one contains pastries. Some habits deserve a second chance.
ending-mira.speaker: mira

ending-mira-slow.text: Her first message arrives at 2:07 AM: “For the record, the jellyfish was not my fault.” You smile for the entire ferry ride home. There is plenty of time for the rest.
ending-mira-slow.speaker: mira

ending-jun.text: The next evening, Jun meets you without a toolbox. He looks a little defenseless. You take his hand before the vending machine can offer advice. Dinner is very good. The windows are even better.
ending-jun.speaker: jun

ending-jun-slow.text: The pancakes are exactly as terrible as promised. The conversation lasts three hours. When he asks if you’d like to do this again, neither of you bothers pretending it’s about breakfast.
ending-jun-slow.speaker: jun

ending-crew.text: The clock still stops at 1:59. There is always an extra mug behind the counter. The city calls you a transport irregularity. You prefer “friends.” Sir Quacks-a-Lot has been elected treasurer.
ending-crew.speaker: sable
